title: Controversy status — Reformed concede polity and external ceremonies to Church prudence
source_text: XX. Porro ex iis quae dicta sunt, facile colligi potest quatenus Ecclesiae nostrae cum Ecclesia Romana in hac quaestione conveniant, & quatenus ab ea dissentiant: adeoque quis sit hujus controversiae status. Et primo quidem Ecclesiae Romanae concedimus singula quae pertinent ad Ecclesiae politiam, publicique & externi cultus ceremonias, ex Scriptura peti non posse, sed esse potestati Ecclesiae permissa, & relicta prudentiae praepositorum Ecclesiae.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover from what has been said it can easily be gathered how far our Churches agree with the Roman Church in this question, and how far they dissent from her: and therefore what the state of this controversy is. And first indeed we concede to the Roman Church that the several things which belong to the Church's polity and to the ceremonies of public and external worship cannot be drawn from Scripture, but are left to the Church's power and to the prudence of the Church's overseers.
pass_b_english: From the foregoing, the controversy's state is clear: where Reformed churches agree with Rome, and where they do not.
First concession: polity and public external-worship ceremonies need not be fetched from Scripture; they are left to Church power and her overseers' prudence.

lemmas.gloss: how far they dissent from her
the prudence of the Church's overseers

choices.why: Standard Reformed allowance for indifferent order.
Church officers entrusted with rites, not dogma deposit.
